person: Maribel Santos is a 52-year-old certified coder and biller who works part-time at a three-doctor family practice and freelances for two other offices. Because the practice administrator is out on leave and nobody else will do it, she has been handed the credentialing tracking: three physicians' Medicare revalidations, plan profile attestations and license renewals. She knows claims and denial codes cold but is not sure about revalidation windows or attestation rules, and she distrusts tools that act before they check. She wants nothing submitted, uploaded, attested or paid that she has not seen first, and she wants plain billing words, not app jargon.
stated_up_front: I got stuck with credentialing for our three docs while the administrator's out. Check where each one stands on Medicare revalidation, the plan profiles and license renewal, and tell me what's actually due before you touch anything.

facts.truth: Dr. Helen Okafor, Dr. Ray Delgado and Dr. Priya Raman are the three current doctors; Dr. Tom Whitby left the practice in August 2026.
He sent a separation notice effective August 31, 2026 and it is saved in the shared drive; he withdrew the practice's access to his profile.
The posted due date is March 31, 2027, which is inside the seven-month window, so she can revalidate now.
The posted due date shows TBD, so nothing should be submitted for him yet.
The practice's group enrollment was submitted on October 2, 2026 and is still in review, so it must not be resubmitted.
Her license expires January 31, 2027, so the 60-day window opens December 2, 2026 and renewal now would be too early.
She has 28 of the 40 required CME hours on her transcript, so her license cannot be renewed on sworn hours yet.
Dr. Delgado's folder holds last year's expired certificate (expired June 30, 2026) and an unbound renewal quote from the carrier; the bound certificate has not arrived.
Dr. Okafor attested June 20, 2026 and Dr. Raman attested July 15, 2026; both are past or near the 120-day mark.
Anything sent, attested or paid goes through the practice administrator, Gwen Pruitt, when she's back, but Maribel can approve small things herself.

unknowns: Why Dr. Delgado's Medicare due date shows TBD and when it will be posted
Whether the carrier has bound Dr. Delgado's renewal coverage yet
The exact rule for how many days before expiry the board lets a license be renewed
Whether the DMEPOS-style three-year cycle applies to anything the practice has enrolled
